subject: Re: Contract amendment request — EU onboarding + APAC warm-standby and data guardrails
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@evrinlabs.it>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Oct 2027 14:23:00 +0200
Subject: Contract amendment request — EU onboarding + APAC warm-standby

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the ongoing support — Evrin's leadership is ready to move forward on a 12-month renewal but with two changes we need to lock in during the amendment:

1) EU primary residency: We need production traffic to be served from EU-only nodes for EU customers (GDPR requirements).
2) APAC warm-standby: We want APAC as a warm-standby region for scale and DR, with automatic cross-region failover for latency spikes >2s and a tested quarterly failover window.

Can you share a sketch SOW, ballpark pricing for dedicated vCPU/GPU capacity, and any additional guardrails you require for DPA/KMS? We'll need an internal review with procurement next week.

Tom Nguyen (cc) will handle procurement questions.

Appreciate a quick outline — we have a board decision deadline at the end of October.

Best,
Elena
Head of Platform
Evrin Labs

--
Attachment: none (initial ask)

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@evrinlabs.it>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Oct 2027 16:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Contract amendment request — EU onboarding + APAC warm-standby

Elena — thanks for the clear ask. High level plan below and I've attached a SOW skeleton to start (EVR-SOW-draft-20271015.pdf):

- EU primary: enable EU single-tenant node group with customer key separation. Data at rest remains in EU region; we provide a DPA addendum and support KMS integration (customer-managed keys) — SOC2 evidence attached in later thread.
- APAC warm-standby: warm-standby pool with autoscale; failover policy can be configured to trigger on p99 latency and error rate thresholds. We run quarterly failover drills that we document and share results.
- Timeline: target EU pilot in 8 weeks, full production in 12 weeks post-signature (subject to model rollback testing).
- Commercials: recommend a 12-month amendment with a blended committed capacity + burst pool. I'll get a pricing sheet from Dylan and detailed capacity scenarios from Ben.

Next step: quick sync call Monday to align timeline and procurement asks? I'm copying Marissa (AM) and Ben (CSM) so they can scope.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

- EU single-tenant node (data residency + customer-managed KMS) — estimate commit sizing and uplift for EU nodes.
- APAC warm-standby (hot caches disabled, KV warmup strategy) — capacity to hold KV cache for quick failover.
- Quarterly failover drill support (engineering hours + runbook updates).

Please review the attached capacity scenarios (capacity-scenarios-evr-20271016.xlsx) and return a recommended commercial (committed vs burst) and an SLO we can commit for failover windows (we should avoid hard 100% uptime RTOs).

Would prefer numbers by EOD Monday so I can respond before Evrin's procurement review.

—Lauren

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 08:31:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Contract amendment request — EU onboarding + APAC warm-standby

Hi Elena / Lauren,

Following Lauren's note, here's a technical + commercial summary (high level):

Technical:
- EU node group: We provision a dedicated EU node pool (multi-AZ where available) with customer-provided KMS support. Data at rest and primary KV cache will remain in EU for EU-routed sessions.
- APAC warm-standby: We maintain a warm pool in APAC with persistent KV snapshotting every 15 minutes; on failover we replay the latest snapshot and rebuild in ~90s for the KV layer, model warmup target ~3–4s added latency during first tokens.
- Failover policy: configurable p99 latency threshold (default 2s) + error rate + manual canary step. We propose quarterly DR drills with a formal runbook and shared postmortem.

Commercial (ballpark):
- 12 mo amendment: base commit covering EU node pool (equivalent to 2x base capacity) + APAC warm standby reserve. Estimated uplift: +22% on your current committed spend; burst consumption billed at standard burst rates.
- Technical professional services: 8 engineer-days for onboarding, 4 engineer-days per quarterly drill (optional add-on).

Attachments: SOC2-Type2-Redacted-2027.pdf, network-arch-evr-eu-node.png, capacity scenarios (already shared).

If that aligns, Lauren can draft an amendment and I can scope the onboarding project plan with SRE.

Best,
Ben Carter
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: SOC2-Type2-Redacted-2027.pdf; network-arch-evr-eu-node.png

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@evrinlabs.it>

Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 13:02:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Contract amendment request — EU onboarding + APAC warm-standby

Thanks Ben and Lauren — that's exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple of procurement asks / redlines from our side (attached term-sheet):

- Add a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) referencing EU data residency and customer KMS controls.
- SLA for cross-region failover: we want a documented RTO target for failover initiation (we're asking for a 5 minute max initiation window and post-failover verification within 30 minutes). Appreciate that full restoration to 100% throughput may take longer; include runbook and quarterly drill deliverables.
- Pricing: can you include a not-to-exceed uplift for the first 90 days during pilot so we can model budget?

I've attached a redlined term-sheet for amendment review. Procurement is standing by for a draft amendment and SOW.

Elena

--
Attachment: EVR-Termsheet-Redlines-20271018.pdf

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@evrinlabs.it>, procurement@evrinlabs.com
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 09:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Contract amendment request — EU onboarding + APAC warm-standby

Elena / Procurement team — appreciate the clear redlines. We can accommodate the DPA/KMS requirement and will build the DPA language into the amendment. Responses to your asks below: 

- DPA/KMS: Confirmed. We'll include customer-managed KMS; data-at-rest residency for EU sessions is an explicit contractual obligation.
- Failover SLA: We can commit to a 5-minute failover initiation window (monitoring detection + automated routing) and verification checks within 30 minutes. We'll exclude full throughput restoration from the SLA but include mandatory quarterly drills and runbook delivery.
- Pricing guardrail: We'll include a not-to-exceed uplift cap for the pilot (first 90 days) equal to +30% of baseline committed spend; any material overage above that triggers mutual review.

Next steps (action items):
1) I'll circulate a contract amendment draft + updated SOW (EVR-Contract-Amendment-20271018.docx).
2) Ben will produce the onboarding project plan and a schedule for the first quarterly drill.
3) Marissa will set a dates for a procurement + legal 30-minute sync to finalize DPA clauses.

If that sounds good I'll target sending the amendment and SOW by end of day Wednesday so you have time for the procurement review.

Thanks all — looking forward to getting this locked in.

Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

--
